content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use present simple forms for regular work and study facts. Model: “I work at a shop, and my sister studies at home.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use workday facts clearly and politely. One useful response is: “I work at a shop, and my sister studies at home.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where workday facts is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about workday facts.

listening.question: What does the speaker study?

pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Make the third-person ending in works /s/ clear. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Make the third-person ending in works /s/ clear.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about workday facts.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using workday facts; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise workday facts?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: I work at a shop, and my sister studies at home.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about workday facts with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about workday facts. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: I work at a shop, and my sister studies at home. Submit your draft first.
